user.title: Connect ESP32 displays
user.description: One connection for all panels. The panels only talk to this integration and need no Home Assistant token - each one gets its own device code later. Add the panels afterwards.

data_description.ha_url: How the panels reach Home Assistant, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:8123
data_description.sidebar: Adds an ESP32 Display entry to the sidebar (administrators only) with the layout editor, so no dashboard card is needed.

data_description.ha_url: How the panels reach Home Assistant. With a new address the panels have to be set up again.
data_description.sidebar: Adds an ESP32 Display entry to the sidebar (administrators only) with the layout editor, so no dashboard card is needed.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Only one ESP32 Display connection is needed - add more panels to it.

user.title: Add display
user.description: The display gets its own device code, shown afterwards in the card under “Setup”. Design the layout with the ESP32 Display card.

data_description.name: e.g. Kitchen
data_description.rotation: How the display is mounted. Try another setting if the picture is upside down or sideways. The layout is fitted automatically on a change; the touch calibration stays valid.
data_description.click: A short click from the buzzer on every touch of a button, switch or other control (needs the buzzer on the board). Can also be switched in the editor.
data_description.hw_manage: Set controller, pins and clock here instead of on the display. The next page asks for the values; the display stores them and restarts when they changed. Leave off to keep the settings made in the display's own setup page.

data_description.name: The name comes from the server - the panel does not need changing.
data_description.new_key: Locks out the display that has the old code; it has to be set up again.
data_description.rotation: How the display is mounted. Try another setting if the picture is upside down or sideways. The layout is fitted automatically on a change; the touch calibration stays valid.
data_description.click: A short click from the buzzer on every touch of a button, switch or other control (needs the buzzer on the board). Can also be switched in the editor.
data_description.hw_manage: Set controller, pins and clock here instead of on the display. The next page asks for the values; the display stores them and restarts when they changed. Leave off to keep the settings made in the display's own setup page.

hardware.title: Hardware of the display
hardware.description: Sent to the display when it connects. A wrong value usually leaves the screen black, but WiFi and this connection keep working, so you can correct it here. Pins are GPIO numbers; -1 means not connected.

data.use_preset: Use the controller's recommended clock and colours

data_description.panel: Chip on the display module. Wrong controller = black or garbled screen.
data_description.use_preset: Sets write/read clock, colour order and inversion to the recommended values of the chosen controller and ignores the fields below for those.
data_description.mosi: SPI data line, shared by display and touch.
data_description.miso: SPI data from the display/touch; input-only pins are fine.
data_description.rst: -1 if the display reset is not wired.
data_description.write_mhz: Lower it first if the screen is black or shows streaks (10 MHz works on the author's board).
data_description.bl_invert: Only for modules with an inverted backlight driver.
data_description.bgr: Switch if red and blue are swapped.
data_description.invert: Switch if the picture looks like a negative.
data_description.touch_on: Switch off for modules without touch.
data_description.touch_cs: Chip select of the touch chip.
data_description.touch_irq: -1 = not wired; the touch is polled over SPI.

error.name_too_long: The name may be at most 31 characters (umlauts count double).
error.name_taken: A display with this name already exists.
error.hw_pin_unusable: {pin}: GPIO {gpio} cannot be used (flash, UART or BOOT pin, or it does not exist).

beep.name: Beep
beep.description: Plays a tone on the buzzer of a display.

preset.name: Preset
preset.description: A ready-made sound. When set, frequency and duration are ignored.

frequency.name: Frequency
frequency.description: Pitch in Hz (100 to 5000). The buzzer is loudest around 2000 to 3000 Hz.

duration_ms.name: Duration
duration_ms.description: Length of the tone in milliseconds (10 to 2000).

repeat.name: Repeat
repeat.description: How often the sound plays (1 to 10, with a short pause in between). All together at most 5 seconds.

no_target.message: Choose a display (device or one of its entities).
